key_terms.يُسْمِنُ: to make fat / to nourish substantially

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when sustenance neither nourishes nor banishes hunger?
ai.summary: In Shia hadith literature, this phrase is often cited to critique material wealth that lacks barakah (divine blessing), rendering it spiritually empty and physically insufficient despite its quantity. It underscores the principle that true sustenance (rizq) is measured by its capacity to nourish the soul and satisfy essential needs, rather than mere accumulation. This teaching aligns with the ethical imperative to seek provision that is both halal and beneficial, avoiding the trap of hoarding without gratitude.
